title: Chile: History & Governance Update — Wed Aug 26, 2026
summary: Kast's ACOT constitutional security reform, signed August 10 to create a new 240-day presidential state of exception, drew mounting cross-partisan backlash through late August. Cadem polling shifted from 58% opposed to unilateral presidential power (Aug 20) to 49% opposed with Kast's disapproval at 57% (Aug 24). title: Chile: History & Governance Update — May 24, 2026
summary: Chile's Chamber of Deputies passed the base text of President Kast's flagship economic reconstruction bill 90-59-1 on May 20, cutting the corporate tax rate from 27% to 23% — but the contested 25-year tax stability clause faces an uncertain path in the Senate. In parallel, a joint Army-Carabineros-PDI operation arrested Mapuche werkén Jorge Huenchullán at Temucuicui by helicopter on May 19; a Collipulli court ordered preventive detention on May 20 with prosecutors seeking 18 years. The Huenchullán family issued a formal denunciation on May 23 accusing the state of a 'racist structure' that criminalizes the community. A Codelco internal audit revealed a 27,000-tonne production overstatement — the state copper giant's true 2025 output is the lowest since 1998 — with an executive fired and $14.3 million in bonuses clawed back. Q1 2026 GDP contracted 0.5% as copper output fell 5.8%. Kast's approval fell to approximately 26% on Day 70, with 66% of Chileans skeptical the reform will revive the economy.

title: Chile: History & Governance Update — May 09, 2026
summary: José Antonio Kast's first months as Chile's most conservative president since Pinochet have been turbulent: his approval crashed from 59% to 29% within weeks of taking office following fuel price hikes of 32–62%, triggering the largest cacerolazos since the 2019 estallido. Student protests erupted in Santiago on April 29 against education budget cuts, while May Day marches saw CUT-led union demands for wage protection. Business confidence fell below the 50-point pessimism threshold in April. On the positive side, lithium exports nearly tripled year-on-year with Q1 revenue hitting $1.108 billion — up 147.7% — as the Codelco–Rio Tinto partnership ramps production at Maricunga and Nuevo Cobre. The IMF's May 4 Article IV mission flagged fuel-driven inflation risks while acknowledging Chile's structural strengths.
